solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pontoon containing large container for tuna

indicators.note: a thing containing another holds it inside, so the card game's name is split around the vessel

blocks.note: pontoon is the British name for the card game blackjack
a skip is a large open builder's container for rubbish

explanation.surface: A floating pontoon carrying a big box of tuna, as at a fish market.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is not a floating platform but the British name for the card game. A skip is a British builder's rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: The black skipjack is a species of small tuna found in warm Pacific waters.

clue.text: Liberally non-exclusive statesman loses badly in pursuit of crumpet?

indicators.note: loses tells us the statesman's name drops some letters

blocks.note: crumpet is British slang for an attractive woman, as is broad in American slang
Winston Churchill, the wartime prime minister
ill as an adverb means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A liberal politician fails miserably while chasing a teacake.
explanation.walkthrough: In pursuit of means coming after, so the shortened statesman follows. A crumpet is a British griddle cake, and also slang for a desirable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad church is a group, originally the tolerant wing of the Anglican Church, that admits a wide range of views.

clue.text: Buzzing centre of Innisfree aglow — essential for cabinbuilder

indicators.note: the centre of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter
buzzing suggests a whirl of excited activity, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: the middle of the nine letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Yeats's Lake Isle of Innisfree, all bees and glow, where he would build a small cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem has a 'bee-loud glade' and 'noon a purple glow', and the poet will 'a small cabin build there'. A log-saw does buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: A log-saw cuts timber into logs, the basic tool for anyone putting up a log cabin.

clue.text: Night raid in dark reached environs

indicators.note: environs are the surroundings, so the verb surrounds the other pieces

blocks.note: came to, arrived at
I as a short form of in
sad of a colour means dark or sombre

explanation.surface: An attack by night, carried out under cover of darkness on the surrounding area.
explanation.walkthrough: CAME surrounds I and SAD. Sad for a colour meaning dark is in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisade was a night attack, the raiders wearing shirts over their armour to recognise one another.

clue.text: Loop in thread? There's work replacing it in weave

indicators.note: replacing means one piece is swapped in where another stood

blocks.note: to knit is to weave yarn
taken as written, the letters taken out
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A knitter finds a loop in the yarn and has to rework it in the weave.
explanation.walkthrough: OP takes the place of IT in KNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A knop is a knob or loop made in yarn for decorative effect, a fancy effect in thread.

clue.text: Monarch accepts wretched p-penance (not new), form of torture

indicators.note: accepts means taking something in, so the monarch holds the rest
wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters are knocked about
not new says the letter standing for new is dropped

blocks.note: a king is a monarch
the stuttered word taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A king stammers out his penance, a torment of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in p-penance is not just surface: the doubled P is needed. Only one of its two Ns goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneecapping is the punishment of shooting someone in the knee, a form of torture used by paramilitaries.

clue.text: Line from Spenser retained in head once — early part of a cycle?

indicators.note: retained in means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: pash is an old word for the head
rew is Spenser's spelling of row, a line

explanation.surface: A verse by Spenser stuck in an old memory, from early in the poem sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' suggests a cycle of poems like Spenser's; it is the washing machine's.
explanation.definitionFit: A prewash is the first stage of a washing machine's programme, before the main wash.

clue.text: Examinations I sat, worried about university degree

indicators.note: worried means fretted over and pulled about, so the letters are shuffled
about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next pieces

blocks.note: the letters of I sat rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university
D is the abbreviation for degree

explanation.surface: A student recalls the exams they sat, anxious about a university degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Examinations' looks like school tests; here they are financial inspections.
explanation.definitionFit: Audits are official examinations of accounts, inspections checking that records are correct.

clue.text: Raven, its head stuck in cattle food?

indicators.note: its head points to the first letter of the bird just named
stuck in means lodged inside, so the letter goes into the feed

blocks.note: cattle cake is compressed feed for livestock
the first letter of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A raven caught with its head in a cattle trough.
explanation.walkthrough: Raven does double duty, as definition and as the source of R.
explanation.definitionFit: Crake is a dialect word for a crow or raven, related to croak.

clue.text: Lock (old) on major river put to the test — it's important for nation's economy

blocks.note: key in an old sense meant a lock or fastening
the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
to try is to test

explanation.surface: An old canal lock on a big river being tested, vital to a country's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A key industry is one central to a country's economy, such as steel or energy.

clue.text: One tragically loved from afar, near distraught about love kiss

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so these letters are thrown into disorder
about means surrounding, so the jumbled word wraps round the next pieces

blocks.note: the letters of near rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A lovesick admirer, close by but beside themselves, longing for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Roxane is the woman Cyrano de Bergerac loves at a distance in Rostand's play, dying before he can declare it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rostand's play Cyrano adores his cousin Roxane secretly from afar, a famously tragic unspoken passion.

clue.text: Stumble on, eyes partly losing what's central to each

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its middle letters

blocks.note: taken as written; losing its middle YE leaves its ends
taken as written; losing its middle ARTL leaves its ends

explanation.surface: Tripping over things because your eyes are only half working.
explanation.walkthrough: With centres removed, EYES leaves ES and PARTLY leaves PY.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, and stumble on means to find by chance, the same discovery.

clue.text: Rib from Edward the Fifth found in damaged urn, English

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another, here inside the damaged vessel
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: urn rearranged
ER is Edward Rex, the royal cipher, and V the Roman numeral five
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A bone of Edward V, one of the Princes in the Tower, turns up in a broken burial urn.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward V was the boy king who vanished in the Tower; the royal cipher ER plus the Roman numeral gives his tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervure is a rib or vein in an insect's wing or a leaf, so it is a rib in the biological sense.

clue.text: Early inscription carved in log, amorous

indicators.note: letters carved in something are cut into it, so the answer lies within the following words

blocks.note: runs across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: An ancient love message cut into a log, like initials carved in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogam, or ogham, is the early Irish alphabet of strokes, cut on stones in inscriptions from about the fourth century.

clue.text: Home counties sale, always for a week

blocks.note: the Home Counties are the counties round London, in the South East of England
vend as a noun means a sale
ay, or aye, is an old word for ever

explanation.surface: A shop in the Home Counties advertising a sale that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London. AY for 'always' survives in 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seven-day lasts for seven days, a week, as with a seven-day pass or ticket.

clue.text: Sleep rough, being in charge of vessel

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang verb for sleeping out in barns or doorways
second meaning: a person, a being, who commands a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor bedding down rough while still responsible for the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb but is the noun: a creature who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain of a boat, and to skipper is old slang for dossing outdoors or in a barn.

clue.text: Miller's work, grinding rice with club

indicators.note: grinding breaks things up, so these letters are crushed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of rice and club rearranged

explanation.surface: A miller at work, grinding rice with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The miller is the playwright Arthur Miller, not a grinder of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible is Arthur Miller's 1953 play about the Salem witch trials.

clue.text: Spoke with outsiders in exchange? It gives orator a lift

indicators.note: the two outer letters change places, a small reshuffle of the word's letters

blocks.note: spoke in the sense of uttered

explanation.surface: Someone talking with strangers during a trade, then a line about lifting a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first and last letters of SAID and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform, so it literally lifts a speaker above the audience.

clue.text: Sow maybe protecting her smallest offspring in tent of skins

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so the tent encloses the offspring

blocks.note: a ger is a Mongolian felt or skin tent, a yurt
the runt is the smallest of a litter

explanation.surface: A mother pig shielding the weakest piglet inside a hide shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunter is a pig, named for its noise, and a sow is one example.

clue.text: The old encourage painting etc in one who's timid

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here inside the timid person

blocks.note: a hen is a timid, fussy person, as in hen-hearted
art covers painting and its fellow disciplines

explanation.surface: Elderly people urging a shy person to take up painting and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an obsolete form: harten is the old spelling of hearten.
explanation.definitionFit: Harten is an archaic form of hearten, meaning to give courage or cheer to someone.

clue.text: Ran wild? It's captured by section of poem in anthology

indicators.note: running wild is out of control, so these letters lose their order
something captured is held inside its captor

blocks.note: a passus is a canto or division of a medieval poem
ran rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild run, perhaps a line escaping from a poem, caught in a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for the shuffled word itself, the fodder. Passus is the term for the sections of Piers Plowman.
explanation.definitionFit: Parnassus, the mountain of the Muses, is also a name for a collection of poems, as in Emerson's Parnassus.

clue.text: Woodland umbellifer, place to put disguised gin in

indicators.note: something disguised is changed in appearance, so its letters are rearranged
place is the instruction to set one thing into another, completed by the in at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
gin rearranged

explanation.surface: A woodland plant, and a handy spot for hiding a bottle of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to put' reads as a noun phrase, a hiding spot; in fact place ... in is an order to insert, with the final 'in' completing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pignut, or earthnut, is a woodland plant of the carrot family with an edible tuber.

clue.text: Take special care of lettuce plant

blocks.note: cos is a long-leaved lettuce, the romaine
to set is to plant

explanation.surface: A gardener tending a lettuce seedling with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or coddle, treating someone with special care.

clue.text: Brigand controlled this kingdom round heart of China

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter
round means surrounding, so the verb goes round the central letter

blocks.note: had in the sense of held or possessed
the fifth of five letters' middle, the centre of china
the United Kingdom, where the setter writes

explanation.surface: A bandit who once ruled Britain and pivoted around China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This kingdom' is the setter's own country, the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiduks were Balkan outlaws who fought the Ottomans; the word came to mean any brigand.

clue.text: What's inflamed anti-Gaddafi revolution in part?

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, a run inside them

blocks.note: runs across the end of the name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Asking what set the Libyan uprising against Gaddafi alight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2011 Libyan uprising against Colonel Gaddafi was topical when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means burning, on fire, and inflamed is its figurative or literal equivalent.

clue.text: Line coming up, catwalk's last — it was enveloped in white

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top
last points to the final letter of the word before

blocks.note: a ley is a line, as in ley line
the final letter of catwalk

explanation.surface: A model coming up the catwalk last, dressed all in white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was' marks an obsolete word: yelk is an old form of yolk, which sits inside the egg white.
explanation.definitionFit: The yolk of an egg is surrounded by the albumen, the white, so it is what is enveloped there.

clue.text: Garment tenor finally removed, becoming focus of attention

indicators.note: removed at the end means a letter is dropped from the word's tail

blocks.note: clout is an old word for a cloth or piece of clothing
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A singer whips off a piece of clothing and becomes the centre of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T from the end of CLOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clou is French for nail, borrowed for the chief point of interest or star attraction.

clue.text: Eucharistic element that is kept in glasses

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, here inside the glasses

blocks.note: specs is short for spectacles
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Communion wine, which is held in drinking glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' suggests wine glasses at Communion; here they are spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology the species are the bread and wine of the Eucharist, the visible forms of the sacrament.

clue.text: Farm produce as rent I kept in tin

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, here inside the container

blocks.note: a can is a tin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant farmer pays the rent in produce stored in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain, or kain, was rent paid in kind with farm produce, chiefly in Scotland.

clue.text: Trailing at sea? Light sail raised abaft

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of trailing rearranged

explanation.surface: A sail streaming behind a ship on the ocean, hoisted at the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtail is a small studding sail set on a gaff, extending beyond the stern of a ship.

clue.text: What makes bed dry (when spread)? Fibre matting

indicators.note: the two letters are spread apart to make room for a piece between them

blocks.note: B stands for bed, as in B and B
as in the sense of while or when
T for teetotal, as in TT

explanation.surface: Asking what will keep a bed dry, answered with woven mats.
explanation.walkthrough: B and T, from bed and dry, are spread to take AS. The question also hints that bast mats can line a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bast is the fibrous inner bark of lime and other trees, used to weave mats, so matting fibre.

clue.text: Pig's trotter, raw (as the French have it) with e.g. haricot, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear points to a word picked up by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: cru is French for raw
a haricot is a kind of bean

explanation.surface: A cookery note on raw pork served with beans, French style.
explanation.definitionFit: Crubeen is an Irish dish of boiled pig's feet, from the Irish word crúibín, a little hoof.

clue.text: Regardless of care, claret in vat that's in good condition

indicators.note: regardless of means leaving aside, so those letters are dropped
in places the remainder inside the vat

blocks.note: a kier is a large vat used for bleaching cloth
the red wine of Bordeaux, taken as written
taken as written, the letters to drop

explanation.surface: Ignore the worry: the wine in the vat is in fine shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Each letter of care comes out of the wine, leaving just two letters. A kier is a dyer's or bleacher's vat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilter means proper working order, usually heard in the idiom out of kilter.

clue.text: Not exactly eighteen yet, or … being in different parts

indicators.note: not exactly signals the words are not as they stand but must be reworked

blocks.note: every letter of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone not quite eighteen yet, and so on, trailing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterogeneity is the state of being made of dissimilar elements, a mixture of different parts.
